cards.title: Introduction to Java Arrays
cards.content:
In Java, an array is a container object that holds a fixed number of values of a single type. The length of an array is established when the array is created, and after creation, its length is fixed.

To declare an array, you define the data type followed by square brackets:

int[] numbers;
String[] names;

To allocate memory for the array, use the new keyword:

numbers = new int[5]; // Allocates memory for 5 integers

content.text: To find the number of elements in an array named 'scores', we access its built-in read-only property: scores.________

cards.title: Memory Allocation & Default Values
cards.content:
When an array is instantiated in Java, memory is allocated on the heap. The elements of the array are automatically initialized with default values depending on their data type:

  • Numeric types (int, double, etc.): 0 or 0.0
  • boolean: false
  • Object references (String, custom classes): null
boolean[] flags = new boolean[3]; // elements: [false, false, false]
String[] words = new String[2];  // elements: [null, null]

cards.title: Iterating through Arrays
cards.content:
You can traverse arrays using a standard for loop or an enhanced for-each loop.

Standard for loop: Ideal when you need access to the index.

for (int i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
    System.out.println(arr[i]);
}

Enhanced for loop (for-each): Cleaner syntax when you only need to read the elements sequentially.

for (int element : arr) {
    System.out.println(element);
}

cards.title: Multidimensional Arrays
cards.content:
In Java, multidimensional arrays are actually arrays of arrays. This means each row can have a different length, creating what is known as a jagged array.

Syntax to declare and initialize a standard 2D array (matrix):

int[][] matrix = new int[3][4]; // 3 rows, 4 columns

Defining a jagged array:

int[][] jagged = new int[2][];
jagged[0] = new int[3]; // Row 0 has 3 columns
jagged[1] = new int[5]; // Row 1 has 5 columns

cards.title: The java.util.Arrays Class
cards.content:
Java provides a utility class named java.util.Arrays containing static methods for common operations like sorting, searching, and printing arrays:

  • Arrays.toString(arr): Prints 1D array elements cleanly.
  • Arrays.deepToString(arr): Prints nested (multidimensional) arrays.
  • Arrays.sort(arr): Sorts elements in natural ascending order.
  • Arrays.binarySearch(arr, key): Quickly searches for a key (array must be sorted first).

pairs.value: Locates the index of an item in a sorted array
Clones or resizes an array into a new reference

cards.title: Key Takeaways & Limitations
cards.content:
To wrap up, keep these core behaviors in mind as a Java Developer:

  • Fixed Size: You cannot resize an array after initialization. If you need dynamic sizing, use ArrayList.
  • Performance: Arrays provide O(1) direct access time when retrieving an element by index.
  • Type Safety: Arrays are strongly typed. You cannot store a String in an int[].
  • Index Rules: Valid indices range from 0 to length - 1. Accessing outside this bounds throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
